clauses.reason: Section 1(a) establishes the Commission and its membership. EO 11410 (signed 1968-05-06; no effective-date clause) replaced the last sentence, which designated one member from private life as Chairman, with a sentence that one of the members shall be designated by the President as Chairman, so the chairman need no longer come from private life. clauses.reason: Section 3 (the fellows' service) was rewritten three times and continues as amended. Original: appointment for approximately fifteen months on the White House Office, the Vice President's office or the offices of the heads of the ten executive departments, beginning on or about June 1, with stipends from private nonprofit organizations approved by the Commission. EO 11648 section 3 (1972-02-16) restated it for 12 months on the White House staff, the Executive Office, the Vice President's office or Cabinet offices, beginning September 1 (the stipend sentence is not in the restated text). EO 11946 section 2 (1976-10-25) restated it again to add offices of other executive branch officials designated by the President and the Commission. EO 12653 (1988-09-29) struck the words 12 months, beginning and inserted a period set by the Commission not exceeding 365 days, extensions of up to 90 days and a September start; its text applies to Fellows with appointments commencing on or after September 1, 1987. The substance of the section changed; flagged for the reviewer.

research_rationale:
EO 11183 (29 FR 13633, signed 1964-10-03; held official Federal Register text, page location high) establishes the President's Commission on White House Fellowships (section 1: membership, chairman, service at the President's pleasure), directs it to prescribe standards and procedures and recommend candidates (section 2, with the selection criteria in 2(b) and the non-discrimination rule in 2(c)), sets the fellows' service (section 3) and requires federal agency and Civil Service Commission assistance (section 4). It rests on the President's authority as President; no authority statute is involved. The held original has no sunset, expiry or revocation. Later instruments that change its text, all held in official Federal Register form: EO 11410 (1968-05-06), EO 11648 (1972-02-16), EO 11946 (1976-10-25), EO 12012 (1977-10-03), EO 12107 section 2-101 (signed 1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) and EO 12653 (1988-09-29). None revokes the order; EO 12012 section 3 deletes the age limits of section 2(b)(4), which is the only clause end. The Commission is an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act and lasts only while continued by presidential order; the held biennial continuance orders list it, and the most recent three are EO 14048 (signed 2021-09-30, continued or reestablished until 2023-09-30), EO 14109 (signed 2023-09-29, until 2025-09-30) and EO 14354 (signed 2025-09-29, 90 FR 48145, continued until September 30, 2027), so the Commission was continued through the cutoff date 2026-10-14 without a gap since 2021. Earlier held continuance orders (1975 to 2019) also list the Commission and neither amend nor end any clause; they are not itemised. The OFR disposition record held in jobs/peano-formulario lists the same amendments and continuances and no revocation. Cutoff limit: no held source reaches past the Federal Register publication of EO 14354 for later presidential action; the ofr_catalog and later-source searches were run before the packet was frozen and cannot show an order signed between that freeze and 2026-10-14.
